reviewDecisions.rationale: Formal licensing is a real regime change, but company earnings conversion and prior absorption must be tested.
Near-term demand damage and longer-term localization pressure point in different directions and require decomposition.
Strategic-policy repricing is observable, but the absence of a concrete export/production action makes it an excellent fail-closed test.
Explicit implementation/expiry dates make this a direct test of the new base-horizon convexity route.
Concrete project lists and construction rules can create order visibility, but company/product mapping must be narrow.
The physical price signal is real but still early enough that future severity cannot be assumed.
Keep the product downcycle separate from localization narratives and test whether fail-closed remains correct.
